item.title: Without manufacturing $1tr economy is an illusion
item.description: By Dele Sobowale Japan in fact offers a relevant historical example of what can happen to an economy which falls behind in the global manufacturing race. Even in Africa, the Giant of Africa is lagging behind at least three other economies in the scale and scope of manufacturing. Consequently, the politically-motivated promise to make Nigeria a one trillion dollar economy by 2030 is only one of the many illusions of the Tinubu administration. Desirable as it is, a $1 trillion economy is unachievable for reasons too numerous to discuss now, but, the cardinal reason is Nigeria’s weak manufacturing base – forcing us to import thousands of products which we can, with little effort, produce locally. I was a Senior Lecturer/Consultant working with the Nigerian Institute of Management, NIM, in 1992, when Morita wrote the article in which that statement was made. The NIM Library was my second home and office. When not busy teaching courses in Sales, Marketing and General Management, I was in the Library reading and gathering materials for my lectures, as well as my book of quotations, VBQ – which was published in 2007. Japan was the world’s second largest manufacturing economy as well as the second largest economy; and was threatening the American leadership in that regard. Several books were written on the Art of Japanese Management; leading American Business Schools included courses in Japanese business methods in their curricula as compulsory subjects. The Japanese economy was growing at 7 to 10 per cent annually; and projections were made regarding when it would overtake the US as the largest economy globally. China and India were nowhere in sight. Then, something happened. Science and technology brought new products which called for new and modern factories. Western investors, scared by Japan’s growing economic prowess, diverted investments to other Asian economies – South Korea, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and China. Gradually, several South East Asian nations started challenging Japan in sectors such as electronics and ship building. Unnoticeable at first, but the steady erosion of Japanese share of global manufacturing eventually took its toll. Today, the second and third leading manufacturers are China and India. China is now the largest manufacturer; hotly pursued by China. Japan has dropped to the fifth position in global ranking measured in terms of Gross Domestic Productivity, GDP. China, not Japan, is now threatening the US leadership. Manufacturing is the primary reason for that change in the fortunes of nations. Nigeria Is Missing The Boat Once Again “Those who do not remember the past are condemned to repeat it.” George Santayana, 1863-1952, VBQ p 93. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 16, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian naira opened Monday, November 16, 2026, under mild pressure across the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) while maintaining relative stability in the parallel market. At the official window, data published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) shows the NFEM rate referencing ₦1,353.97 per dollar. This follows a ₦7.18 depreciation in the preceding session as corporate foreign exchange obligations and seasonal end-of-year import demand weighed on liquidity. Meanwhile, spot interbank indicators in early morning trading hovered around ₦1,343.35 per dollar as dealers awaited fresh intraday price discovery. In the parallel market, also known as the black market, Bureau De Change (BDC) operators and street dealers in Lagos and Abuja quoted the US dollar at a buying rate of ₦1,380 and a selling rate of ₦1,390. With the official rate standing at ₦1,353.97 and the parallel market selling at ₦1,390, the exchange rate spread between both markets sits at approximately ₦36.03 per dollar. Market analysts note that steady foreign reserve buffers and ongoing CBN market interventions continue to keep the disparity between the official and unofficial segments within a narrow band compared to historical volatility. item.title: 1,960 Flights Cancelled On Sunday Alone, As US Airport Disruption Enters Day Three
item.description: An additional 1,960 flights were cancelled on Sunday alone as the widespread disruption following an extraordinary no-takeoff order issued by US aviation authorities entered its third day on Monday. About 6,000 flights were cancelled at the weekend, leaving thousands of passengers stranded at airports. The ground stop issued Friday afternoon was only the second time such a directive had been issued nationwide in the busy US airspace since planes were grounded following the 9/11 attacks. It was blamed by the Trump administration on a faulty upgrade to communications equipment. As of Sunday evening, more than 55 US-related flights — those traveling within, into or out of the United States — scheduled for Monday were cancelled, according to industry tracker FlightAware. That marked a dramatic shift from the more than 1,960 flights cancelled on Sunday. Passengers wait for updates at a check-in area at Terminal 7 at Los Angeles International Airport, in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. The Trump administration sought to reassure weary flyers as questions remained over how such chaos could unfold in the world’s largest economy, a country that prides itself on its technological prowess. Throughout the weekend, stranded passengers wandered through chaotic airports and sat on floors, waiting for updates or to be rebooked. Officials blamed Friday’s colossal snafu on faulty work to upgrade air traffic control communication cables. President Donald Trump on Sunday ended uncharacteristic days of silence on the ground stop, but only to blame his predecessor Joe Biden for the debacle. Planes sit idle at Los Angeles International Airport in Los Angeles on November 13, 2026. Trump insisted he inherited a mess from the Biden administration and said Congress, which his party has controlled for two years, must approve funds to upgrade America’s outdated air traffic control system. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump said, referring to the Federal Aviation Administration. “Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began,” Trump asserted. FAA chief Bryan Bedford had said Saturday that air travel for millions of Americans stranded at airports would return to normal by the close of business on Sunday. But Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Sunday morning it will actually take longer to get planes, crews and travelers to where they need to be. “So, in the airspace, we’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Duffy said on ABC News. “We had airplanes and crews out of position because of Friday, so it takes a little bit of time to do that.” Passengers wait in line to retrieve their luggage as flights were cancelled at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in Chicago on November 13, 2026. ‘I’m The Secretary’ Duffy also flatly rejected calls for his resignation over the travel chaos, insisting he inherited woefully outdated air traffi

item.title: Stock market rebounds as investors reap N2.2trn amid decline in oil price
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu The Nigerian stock market rebounded last week after weeks of sustained pressure from profit taking led to decline in stock value. Equity investors on the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX, last week, reaped over N2.2 trillion in capital gains leading the NGX market capitalisation, to close last week at N163.795 trillion, up from N161.593 trillion the previous week. Similarly, another major market performance indicator, NGX All Share Index, ASI, surged by 1.4 % to close at 252,269.16 points from 248,877.22 points the previous week, indicating renewed demand for selected heavyweight stocks, which dominated the market. Analysts noted that although buying interests remained evident in major banking and industrial stocks , the broader market reflected a mixed trading pattern, with investors maintaining selective positions amid intermittent profit-taking in several stocks The positive performance, according to analysts, highlights the continued resilience of the domestic stock market, which has maintained substantial gains since the beginning of the year. Reacting to market performance and outlook analysts at InvestData Consulting Limited, said : “ The immediate market outlook remains cautiously positive, supported by the strong year-to-date return and continued interest in selected large-cap stocks. Nevertheless, investors are likely to maintain a selective approach, considering corporate earnings, dividend expectations, valuation levels and prevailing macroeconomic conditions before increasing their exposure. The possibility of further profit-taking cannot be ruled out, particularly in stocks that have recorded significant gains in recent sessions. Overall, the market appears to be consolidating its recent advances while maintaining an underlying bullish bias. The ability of the index to break above the 255,000-point resistance level, alongside improved market participation, will be important in determining whether the current upward movement can extend into another phase of appreciation.” They further noted that the political outcome of the US midterm elections introduced additional uncertainty into the market adding that the developments have placed renewed attention on the possibility of diplomatic negotiations and their implications for global crude supply. “For Nigeria, the movement in international crude prices remains particularly important given the country’s dependence on oil exports for foreign exchange earnings and government revenue. A sustained decline in crude prices could place additional pressure on projected oil receipts, especially if production levels remain below expectations. Conversely, elevated prices could support external earnings, although the benefits would depend on domestic production performance, export volumes and fiscal management” the analysts added. item.title: Imposing Tinubu in 2027 will trigger crisis — Ex-APC spokesman
item.description: ABUJA — FORMER Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Mr Timi Frank, yesterday, warned that any attempt to force President Bola Tinubu back into office in 2027 could plunge the country into crisis. Read Also: ‘How Tinubu will end insecurity ready’ Frank, who is the Ambassador to East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua, ULMWP, said Nigerians would not accept an outcome that contradicts their votes. “Nigerians will not accept a situation in which someone is declared the winner when the people know they did not vote for him. They should not push the country into a crisis by attempting to impose him on the people,” he warned. Urging the president to abandon his re-election ambition and guarantee a transparent electoral process, he said: “Whoever wins should be allowed to emerge as the choice of the people.” Frank also expressed concern over alleged attempts by some political actors to manipulate the electoral process. He described the public protest against Tinubu after prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, last Friday as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the administration. Tinubu reportedly faced boos from some Hausa protesters who chanted “Ba ma yi” (we don’t want you) after the prayers. In a viral video, some protesters were seen removing and destroying his campaign posters and billboards in parts of Area 1. Frank condemned the protesters for choosing a religious occasion to vent their displeasure and commended the President’s security detail for ensuring his safety and de-escalating the situation. He nevertheless urged the President to recognise the significance of the public reaction. “The rejection was total and unmistakable. No Nigerian president has been embarrassed like this publicly. The way Nigerians rejected him speaks volumes but should he decide to go ahead and he loses, he should be prepared to accept defeat just like former President Goodluck Jonathan did,” he said. The former APC spokesman said he was worried by what he called a growing gap between the assurances given to the President by political associates and the mood of the people. “I have seen the confidence with which some people are assuring President Tinubu that he will win the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, and that he is firmly in control. But the reported embarrassment he suffered during a prayer session in Abuja tells a different story. “What happened in the FCT last Friday showed that political assurances and promises are not necessarily a reflection of the reality on the ground. The public reaction reflects the anger and dissatisfaction of Nigerians, which those around the President may not be telling him about. “What happened in FCT and Jos after the APC rally has shown that people like the FCT minister, Nyesom Wike promising him 80 percent of votes in Abuja and the Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo vowing to give him 2.5 million votes in Edo State, would

item.title: Economy Palava: Traders decry rising waybill ‘store keep’ charges
item.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Small-scale traders operating across major markets in the country have raised the alarm over arbitrary and escalating storage fees, locally known as “store keep money”, charged by transport operators and motor park agents on delayed waybills, warning that the practice is eroding their capital and threatening their livelihoods. For many market women who rely on interstate commercial buses and trucks to restock goods such as foodstuffs, textiles, and household provisions, waybill logistics are the lifeline of daily commerce. However, traders said the shrinking grace periods before daily demurrage charges kick in have turned routine restocking into a financial burden. Economy&Lifestyle visits to some markets revealed a widespread frustration among traders, many of whom operate on thin profit margins and depend on daily turnover or microfinance loans to sustain their stalls. Mrs. Grace Okafor, a wholesale dealer in dried seafood and condiments, recounted how a 24-hour delay caused by heavy rainfall cost her nearly half of her expected profit on a recent consignment. “My goods arrived at the park late in the evening when no one could go out. “By the time I got there the next afternoon with a tricycle to carry my sacks, the park officials insisted I had exceeded their grace period and demanded N6,000 for ‘store keep’. “We cannot increase our selling prices because customers are already struggling to buy. That money came straight out of my capital.” Other traders noted that the lack of standardized billing across motor parks leaves them vulnerable to exploitation, particularly when unforeseen emergencies delay pickup. Mrs. Comfort Momoh, who trades in fabrics and wrappers, stated that arbitrary fee hikes are discouraging traders from ordering goods in bulk. “There is no fixed rate or clear receipt for this store keep money; it depends on the mood of whoever is on duty at the park store,” she said. “Sometimes a driver does not call on time to inform you that the vehicle has arrived, yet the park starts counting storage days against you. By the time you clear your bale, the profit is already gone.” Similarly, Alhaja Rasheedat Suleiman, a palm oil and grain merchant, called on market associations and transport unions to intervene and establish fair, transparent guidelines. “We understand that parks have limited space, but giving traders at least 48 hours of grace after proper notification is only fair,” Alhaja Suleiman said. “Most of us are breadwinners supporting our families from these stalls. If transport companies and park unions do not regulate these charges, many women will be forced out of business.” When contacted, a park supervisor at an interstate loading bay in, who declined to be named, defended the charges, stating that limited warehouse space and the risk of theft or damage make it necessary to compel traders to clear their goods promptly. item.title: Crisis hits Nigeria’s cassava industry with imports rising 13,293% in 5yrs
item.description: *… as Farmers Abandon Farms in 2026 By Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s cassava processing industry is facing a deepening crisis as imports of cassava starch surged by 13,293 per cent in five years, leaving local factories struggling, farmers counting their losses and processors operating at low 15 per cent of their installed capacity. This is happening despite Nigeria’s position as the world’s largest cassava producer as of 2024, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization Corporate Statistical Database, FAOSTAT, an agency of the United Nations. Industry stakeholders attributed the crisis to high production costs, inadequate financing, declining farm acreage and weak enforcement of import restrictions. These factors have made imported alternatives cheaper than locally produced cassava derivatives. The situation has resulted in a glut of raw cassava, falling farm-gate prices, mounting debts among farmers and processors, and growing concerns about the future of local industrial production. Data obtained from the World Bank’s World Integrated Trade Solution, WITS, based on UN Comtrade records, showed that Nigeria’s cassava starch imports rose from 24.1 tonnes in 2020 to 3,227.7 tonnes in 2025, representing a 13,293 per cent increase over five years. A year-on-year breakdown showed that Nigeria imported 24.1 tonnes of cassava starch, valued at $69,440, in 2020. Imports increased by 126.6 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in 2021 to 54.6 tonnes, worth $154,750. In 2022, the volume surged by a further 272.2 per cent YoY to 203.2 tonnes, valued at $292,900. However, following a sharp rise in the exchange rate, imports plunged by 98 per cent YoY in 2023 to 4.1 tonnes, valued at $32,080, before rebounding sharply in 2024 by 73,004.9 per cent to 2,997.3 tonnes, worth $2.34 million. The upward trend continued in 2025, with import volumes rising by 7.7 per cent to 3,227.7 tonnes. However, despite the increase in volume, the value of imports declined by 7.6 per cent to $2.16 million from approximately $2.34 million in 2024. Industry stakeholders, who spoke in exclusive interviews with Financial Vanguard, warned that imports were rising further in 2026 and could continue to increase in subsequent years unless the government addressed the cost disadvantages confronting local processors and strengthened policies supporting domestic production. Farmers, processors count losses The President of Large-Scale Starch and Derivatives Producers Association of Nigeria, LSSDPA, Mrs Oluyemisi Iranloye, who is also the Vice-President of the Industrial Cassava Stakeholders Association of Nigeria, ICSAN, said the crisis had severely affected farmers and processors. Iranloye, founder and Chief Executive Officer of Psaltry International, said farmers could spend about N800,000 cultivating a hectare of cassava but realise only about N300,000 from selling the produce at prevailing farm-gate prices. item.title: Igini to Trump: Tie Nigeria-US relations to credible polls
item.description: A former Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Resident Electoral Commissioner, Mike Igini, has urged US President, Donald Trump, to link America’s immigration policy and diplomatic relations with Nigeria to credible conduct of the country’s 2027 general elections. Read Also: ‘How Tinubu will end insecurity ready’ Igini said electoral malpractice, corruption, insecurity and poor governance were among the factors forcing Nigerians to seek opportunities abroad, arguing that credible elections and accountable leadership could help address the root causes of migration. In an open letter dated November 13, 2026, and addressed to Trump at the White House, the former REC proposed a policy he called the “No Mandate Fraud” Doctrine, urging the US to combine preventive diplomacy, independent election monitoring and targeted sanctions against individuals involved in electoral violations. He argued that border enforcement alone could not address migration without tackling the governance failures driving Nigerians out of their country. “Nigerians are not leaving Nigeria because they do not love their country. They are leaving because of decades of persistent electoral malpractice, corruption, insecurity and weak public accountability that have undermined Nigerians’ confidence in government,” he wrote. Igini urged Trump to send a high-level delegation to engage President Bola Tinubu, political parties, presidential and governorship candidates, INEC and other relevant institutions ahead of the elections. He said the delegation should communicate Washington’s position that credible elections, peaceful political competition and respect for constitutional rights were central to US interests in Nigeria. He also proposed visa restrictions, financial sanctions and asset freezes, where legally justified, against electoral officials found culpable of manipulating results, falsifying records or committing other electoral offences. The former REC extended the call for accountability to judicial officers whose misconduct in electoral cases was established by credible evidence, as well as security personnel involved in voter intimidation, electoral violence and suppression of opposition parties. He identified the police, Department of State Services, Armed Forces and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps as institutions expected to protect voters and ensure impartial enforcement of the law. Igini further urged the US to support credible domestic and international election observers to monitor the process before, during and after the polls, particularly voter intimidation, security neutrality, polling-unit results and transparent collation. Explaining the benefits to Washington, he said credible elections could reduce migration pressure, strengthen security cooperation and create opportunities for stronger economic relations. item.title: We demand impeccable voter register
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, must urgently clean up its battered image by producing an impeccable voters’ register ahead of the 2027 general elections. The discovery that its own officials allegedly compromised the database through fraudulent registrations is a monumental embarrassment. It reinforces existing suspicions about the commission’s impartiality and competence at a time Nigerians desperately need an electoral umpire they can trust. The scale of the problem is alarming. Of the more than 11 million people registered during the 2026 Continuous Voter Registration, CVR, exercise, INEC’s Automated Biometric Identification System, ABIS, flagged approximately 1.5 million entries as suspicious. The commission subsequently removed 1,277,252 invalid records, leaving about 268,000 requiring further verification. The preliminary national register contains over 103.4 million voters. More disturbing is the alleged complicity of registration officers who abused their official login credentials to introduce fictitious identities. They reportedly uploaded AI-generated photographs, reused identical images and exploited registration provisions for persons with disabilities, claiming fictitious applicants had no fingers and could therefore bypass normal fingerprint verification. ABIS detected suspicious facial and biometric inconsistencies during screening. Artificial intelligence has consequently introduced a dangerous dimension toa electoral fraud. Its capacity to generate convincing human faces makes fabricating identities easier and visual inspection less reliable. Although digitally enhanced photographs of genuine applicants are not necessarily fraudulent, fictitious identities must be identified and eliminated. INEC says it has withdrawn implicated officers’ access credentials, commenced investigations, subjected suspicious entries to human adjudication and referred evidence for possible disciplinary action and prosecution. It promises further verification before the final register is displayed on December 15, 2026. These assurances are insufficient without demonstrable accountability. Public confidence in INEC was already fragile before this scandal. Controversies surrounding previous elections, particularly the disputed 2023 presidential election and the failure of IReV to upload results as expected, have deepened distrust. A manipulated register could facilitate fictitious voting identities, impersonation, inflated constituency figures and deliberate disenfranchisement of legitimate voters. Biometric accreditation may prevent some abuses, but cannot excuse a defective database. Professor JoashAmupitan must therefore open the corrective process to independent scrutiny. INEC should partner with opposition parties, civil society organisations, professional technology experts, the media and credible international electoral partners in conducting an independent forensic audit. The commission should publish state-by-state findings

item.title: ASUU Heroes Day, 2027 elections and the futuristic State Police, by Owei Lakemfa
item.description: It was one of the largest gatherings of Africa’s best brains. The date was November 12, the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) 2026 Heroes Day. The academics came from all parts of the country, gathering at the University of Abuja. Amongst them were current and former vice-chancellors, current and past presidents of ASUU, and founding NLC President, Comrade Hassan Sunmonu. There was Alhaji Mahmud Yayale Ahmed, who has held three of the country’s highest public offices: Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Head of the Civil Service, and Minister of Defence. Former Bauchi State Governor AhmaduAdamuMu’azu, ex-Permanent Secretaries Professor GokeAdegoroye and Dr. TimiebiKoripamo-Agary, who, as serving Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Productivity, sued a Minister for conduct bordering on corruption. Minister of State SuwaibaSa’idu Ahmad, a professor of Science Education, held herself up as a proud member of ASUU, identified the principle of good welfare for academics, and urged all to continuously help build bridges between Government and ASUU. The occasion embodied three primary characteristics of the seventy-eight-year-old ASUU. First, ever analysing the past, which is why it annually marks its Heroes Day to honour those who have made sacrifices for the union, universities, and the country. The Day commemorates November 12, 2013, the date former ASUU President and noted novelist Festus Iyayi was killed in a car crash. He was travelling for an ASUU National Executive Council meeting in Kano to find a solution to a national strike triggered by Government’s intransigence and insistence on defunding education. The second ASUU culture is ever interrogating the present, which is why this year’s theme focused on the electoral system. The third is the union’s tendency to probe into the future. This time, it looked at the ongoing attempts to create State Police and the possible impact it could have on the 2027 General Elections. ASUU is also quite strategic in building alliances, which is why its awardees this year included a number of people who led the Government Negotiating Teams or played roles in ensuring the success of the decades-long ASUU-Government negotiations. These included Alhaji Ahmed, Professor MunzaliJibril, whose Negotiating Team in May 2021 broke through barriers and successfully produced a draft agreement, and Professor NimiDimkpa Briggs, who, on June 16, 2022, despite government reservations, followed through with a new draft agreement within ten weeks. The Buhari government had been so displeased with the breakthrough the Briggs Team had made with ASUU that it made false accusations against the likeable professor. It accused him of excluding government agencies from the negotiations, inflating academics’ salaries by N1.1 trillion, and acting out of financial self-interest. item.title: Nigeria: One-party or one-man state? By Suleiman A. Suleiman
item.description: Since at least late 2024, when President Bola Ahmed Tinubu had been in office for barely 18 months, politicians and other Nigerians have been saying that the country is drifting into a one-party state. These warnings have not only grown louder in recent months; they are justified. The All Progressives Congress (APC) now controls 31 out of 36 states, since at least the middle of this year, when the 2027 election campaigns entered top gear. At the end of the 2023 election cycle, the APC controlled 21 states, including the off-cycle election in Edo State in 2024. This means that, in the last year, 10 sitting governors have defected from their original parties to join Tinubu in the APC. The reverse traffic, meanwhile, is zero. This is unlike the 2015 election cycle, when leading politicians were defecting from the then ruling People’s Democratic Party (PDP) to the then main opposition APC. At the same time, the transformation of political organisation and opposition parties that we witnessed during 2013–2015 does not appear to be happening this time, as the leading opposition parties remain ridden by crippling crises that President Tinubu and the APC have been accused of instigating. First of all, the PDP is now a one-man show, and it is difficult to even know what the party stands for or who its leading members are, other than FCT Minister Nyesom Wike. More significantly, in 2023, the Labour Party (LP) and the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) won 63 seats between them—almost all of them for the first time in history—in the National Assembly elections, and a total of 12 states and the FCT in the presidential election by their candidates, Mr Peter Obi and Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso, combined. That was a formidable performance, particularly by Peter Obi, but both the LP and the NNPP are no longer serious contenders in this election, and the two men have since left to meet on the same presidential ticket in the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). Accusing fingers also point to Tinubu for making their own political parties unviable platforms for the two men. This leaves the African Democratic Congress (ADC), which faces the most crisis of all. For almost a year, the ADC, formed by a partial coalition of like-minded and opposition interests, has been held hostage by the antics of one man, enabled almost entirely by Nigerian courts. The status of ADC candidates, from the presidential to the state assembly elections, currently hangs in limbo because Nigerian courts in this era now think that the dubious concerns of one party member are more important than the will of all the voters in the hundreds of primary elections conducted by the APC in the past months. In short, Nigeria today looks like a one-party state, with the ruling APC as the last man standing. In my view, however, Nigeria is not sliding into a one-party state. It is already a one-man state. item.title: PenCom opens up on N52,000 minimum pension guarantee
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The National Pension Commission, PenCom, has shed light on the implementation of the long-awaited Minimum Pension Guarantee, MPG, disclosing that 173,209 Nigerian retirees are eligible to benefit from a guaranteed minimum monthly pension of N52,500 following its formal activation by President Bola Tinubu. The initiative, aimed at improving the welfare and financial security of retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme, CPS, was unveiled alongside a healthcare programme designed to provide free access to essential medical services for low-income pensioners. The two initiatives, the Minimum Pension Guarantee and the Pension Industry Healthcare Plan (PenCare), were announced at the Presidential Pension Security Initiatives ceremony held at the State House Banquet Hall, Abuja. Tinubu, who was represented at the event by Senate President Godswill Akpabio, said the Minimum Pension Guarantee fulfilled a provision of the Pension Reform Act 2004, which was retained in the 2014 legislation but had remained unimplemented for 22 years. Declaring the scheme operational, the President assured pension contributors that the government would no longer allow eligible retirees to receive pensions below the guaranteed minimum threshold. “From this day, there is a floor beneath the Nigerian retiree. No one who contributed under the Contributory Pension Scheme will ever be allowed to fall below,” he said. The President urged successive administrations to sustain the policy and periodically increase the guaranteed amount rather than discontinue it. On the healthcare component, President Tinubu said the Pension Industry Healthcare Plan, PenCare, was designed to shield vulnerable retirees from medical expenses that could deplete their retirement savings. He said beneficiaries would receive healthcare access cards in the coming months, enabling them to access essential medical services without bearing the financial burden. The President also disclosed that his administration had issued a N758 billion bond to address outstanding pension arrears and approved a N32,000 monthly consequential adjustment for affected federal pensioners. He added that state governments had collectively spent more than N1 trillion settling outstanding pension obligationsSpeaking at the ceremony, PenCom Director-General, Omolola Oloworaran, disclosed that 173,209 retirees had qualified for the N52,500 monthly minimum pension. She explained that the beneficiaries comprised 34 per cent of retirees from federal service, 12 per cent from state employment and 54 per cent from the private sector. According to her, the guaranteed amount was determined through actuarial validation and would be reviewed periodically to ensure its sustainability. item.title: Development challenges in Delta: Ebitonmo’s theory of political thermodynamics
item.description: By Enewaridideke Ekanpou Alapala Anthony Ebitonmo, the man currently representing Burutu North Constituency in the Delta State House of Assembly, is again furious, as it is his wont to be, resistant to every benevolent arrester unleashed on him. Rather retrospectively, in a blazing fury, he was recently sighted at Oyangbene and approvingly led into the open arms of people carrying “chalked hearts.” The hearts of Oyangbene people became immediately “chalked” because Ebitonmo was suddenly sighted. Even in their variedly chalked hearts at the sight of the man, they were confounded, thrown off balance, when they were told he had not come for Oyangbene community. Even in their confoundment, they sought to know the rationale behind Ebitonmo’s sudden appearance in Oyangbene when he claimed openly he had not come for the Oyangbene community. In a characteristic blazing fury, he was curtly categorical that his sudden appearance was rooted in two propellants—Serikoromo Primary School and his famed theory named political thermodynamics. Available statistics reveal Serikoromo Primary School in Burutu Local Government Area of Delta State had been the home of rickety structures for decades, daily rendezvoused by pythons, leopards, elephants, lions, grasscutters, lizards, iguanas, rats, cats, and bats. To teachers and pupils, these reptiles and mammals became the bandits troubling them. For decades, they cried their eyes out with tears that spread like the waters of the Atlantic Ocean. However, their impassioned tears looked like the silvery waters in the ocean; they were not comforted like the weeping Biblical Martha. Serikoromo Primary School, founded in 1956, was where I had my primary education in 1988. The oceanic tears of this school had known many decades of neglect. Awakened to the pathetic story of Serikoromo Primary School, Ebitonmo became blazingly furious. With a blazing fury that carried the troubling pains of the poor teachers and pupils, Ebitonmo risked a sudden flight to Serikoromo Primary School without a visible speedboat professionally skimming the white waters of Oyangbene River. His presence in the school was equivalent to ritualistically stepping on “Atu” in a folktale stunningly told by TimiebiMaika. Mystically, as captured in Timiebi’s folktales, ritualistically stepping on the “Atu” was imbued with the power to make one appear dramatically at the backyard of one’s house. The power of invisibility and disappearance dwells mystically in the “Atu” ritual. The second propellant of Ebitonmo’s appearance in Oyangbene without a visible flight was his treasured philosophy of political thermodynamics. Political thermodynamics is the measurable degree of responsiveness of, or applicability of, core developmental ideas to visible development challenges that plague communities and mankind in general. item.title: Businessman, Egungbohun charges African enterprises to connect across boundaries
item.description: Businessman and Chairman of IBD Group, Chief Ibrahim Dende Egungbohun, has urged African entrepreneurs to build businesses that transcend national boundaries, strengthen regional trade and unlock the continent’s vast economic opportunities. Egungbohun made the call following his recognition by BusinessDay Newspaper at its Nigeria Business Leadership Awards (NBLA) 2026, in acknowledgement of his entrepreneurial achievements and IBD Group’s contribution to enterprise development across interconnected economic sectors. The ceremony, held on Friday, November 13, at Victoria Island, Lagos, also marked the newspaper’s 25th anniversary, themed “25 Years of Shaping Impactful Decisions.” Chief Egungbohun was represented by his wife, Chief Mrs Omolara Judith Egungbohun, Chief Executive Officer of IBD Hotels International and other members of the Group’s delegation included staff of IBD Hotels and representatives of IBD Foundation. In his nomination letter, BusinessDay Publisher and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Frank Aigbogun, commended IBD Group’s evolution from agriculture into a diversified enterprise with interests in logistics, construction materials, hospitality and energy. He observed that enterprise development extends beyond establishing businesses to building operating capacity, developing markets, sustaining commercial activities and creating institutions capable of enduring beyond individual transactions. In his remarks, Chief Egungbohun emphasised that Africa’s economic prosperity depended on connecting markets, strengthening commercial relationships and developing businesses capable of operating across geographical boundaries. He said: “Africa cannot unlock its full economic potential through isolated national markets. We must build enterprises that connect production, distribution, investment and trade across geographical boundaries. “At IBD Group, we see agriculture, logistics, hospitality, construction materials and energy as interconnected parts of a wider economic ecosystem. Their integration creates value chains, facilitates trade, attracts investment and generates employment. “Our ambition is to build businesses that contribute not only to national development but also to a more integrated African economy where entrepreneurs can compete, collaborate and create lasting value.” He dedicated the recognition to the Group’s employees, management, partners and stakeholders, acknowledging their collective contributions to its growth. His message resonates with Africa’s regional integration ambitions under the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which seeks to expand intra-African trade and create opportunities for businesses across the continent. item.title: I’m running to complete South’s remaining 4 years — Makinde
item.description: By Dapo Akinrefon LAGOS — PRESIDENTIAL candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, yesterday, revealed that he is contesting the 2027 presidential election to win, reset Nigeria and lead it into a new era of opportunity, security and shared prosperity. Makinde, in a statement by his campaign office, reaffirmed his commitment to a single four-year term, saying this would allow Southern Nigeria to complete its eight-year turn in the presidency by 2031. The campaign office said: “Governor Makinde is seeking the mandate of Nigerians with a clear sense of purpose and a firm commitment to accountable leadership. His ‘Reset Agenda’ is very clear on this. His campaign is already taking that message to citizens in every part of the country. “His commitment to a single four-year term is rooted in his belief that national unity rests on fairness, mutual respect and fidelity to the understandings that hold our federation together. Southern Nigeria should complete its remaining four years in the presidency, bringing its turn to eight years by 2031. “Those four years must count in the lives of Nigerians. His priorities are to restore security, expand opportunities for enterprise and employment, strengthen public institutions and give families confidence in their future. He is seeking a mandate tied to clear priorities and measurable results. “His engagement with political leaders and, indeed, Nigerians of all classes across the country reflects his determination to build the broad support required to win and govern effectively. He brings to those conversations a clear presidential ambition, a commitment to fairness and a programme centred on the welfare of Nigerians. “Makinde is in this contest to earn the people’s trust, win their votes and serve as President for one purposeful four-year term.” Vanguard News The post I’m running to complete South’s remaining 4 years — Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AS FARMERS ABANDON FARMS IN 2026: Crisis hits Nigeria’s cassava industry with imports rising 13,293% in 5yrs
item.description: By Cynthia Alo Nigeria’s cassava processing industry is facing a deepening crisis as imports of cassava starch surged by 13,293 per cent in five years, leaving local factories struggling, farmers counting their losses and processors operating at low 15 per cent of their installed capacity. This is happening despite Nigeria’s position as the world’s largest cassava producer as of 2024, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization Corporate Statistical Database, FAOSTAT, an agency of the United Nations. Industry stakeholders attributed the crisis to high production costs, inadequate financing, declining farm acreage and weak enforcement of import restrictions. These factors have made imported alternatives cheaper than locally produced cassava derivatives. The situation has resulted in a glut of raw cassava, falling farm-gate prices, mounting debts among farmers and processors, and growing concerns about the future of local industrial production. Data obtained from the World Bank’s World Integrated Trade Solution, WITS, based on UN Comtrade records, showed that Nigeria’s cassava starch imports rose from 24.1 tonnes in 2020 to 3,227.7 tonnes in 2025, representing a 13,293 per cent increase over five years. A year-on-year breakdown showed that Nigeria imported 24.1 tonnes of cassava starch, valued at $69,440, in 2020. Imports increased by 126.6 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in 2021 to 54.6 tonnes, worth $154,750. In 2022, the volume surged by a further 272.2 per cent YoY to 203.2 tonnes, valued at $292,900. However, following a sharp rise in the exchange rate, imports plunged by 98 per cent YoY in 2023 to 4.1 tonnes, valued at $32,080, before rebounding sharply in 2024 by 73,004.9 per cent to 2,997.3 tonnes, worth $2.34 million. The upward trend continued in 2025, with import volumes rising by 7.7 per cent to 3,227.7 tonnes. However, despite the increase in volume, the value of imports declined by 7.6 per cent to $2.16 million from approximately $2.34 million in 2024. Industry stakeholders, who spoke in exclusive interviews with Financial Vanguard, warned that imports were rising further in 2026 and could continue to increase in subsequent years unless the government addressed the cost disadvantages confronting local processors and strengthened policies supporting domestic production. Farmers, processors count losses The President of Large-Scale Starch and Derivatives Producers Association of Nigeria, LSSDPA, Mrs Oluyemisi Iranloye, who is also the Vice-President of the Industrial Cassava Stakeholders Association of Nigeria, ICSAN, said the crisis had severely affected farmers and processors. Iranloye, founder and Chief Executive Officer of Psaltry International, said farmers could spend about N800,000 cultivating a hectare of cassava but realise only about N300,000 from selling the produce at prevailing farm-gate prices. item.title: England End Spain’s 44-Game Unbeaten Run With Nations League Win
item.description: England snapped world champions Spain’s unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3. Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat. England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser. Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March. England coach Thomas Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side. Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic. However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly. Spain’s midfielder #09 Fermin Lopez challenges England’s goalkeeper #13 James Trafford during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Thomas COEX / AFP) Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked. Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide. Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time. The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail. De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy. England’s midfielder #17 Morgan Rogers fights for the ball with Spain’s forward #17 Nico Williams during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP) Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence. Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third. La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Elliot Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal. The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty. Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Nico Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in. Williams curled over and Trafford denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record. item.title: 2027 Grammys Nominations To Be Announced Monday
item.description: Nominations for the 69th Annual Grammy Awards, scheduled to hold in February 2027, will be announced on Monday, November 16, with Nigerian music fans able to follow the presentation from 1:45 p.m. West African Time (WAT). The Recording Academy will unveil nominees across all 100 categories during a special presentation led by its Chief Executive Officer, Harvey Mason Jr., and Chair of its Board of Trustees, Dr Chelsey Green. The announcement will begin at 7:45 a.m. Eastern Time (1:45 p.m. WAT), while the complete list of nominees is expected to be published around 9 a.m. Eastern Time (3 p.m. WAT). The presentation will be streamed live on Grammy.com and the official Grammys YouTube channel, with additional coverage on ABC’s Good Morning America. Grammys For the first time, the nominations presentation will also be broadcast live at The Square in Times Square, New York, in partnership with Hilton, the Recording Academy’s official hotel partner. Several Grammy-winning and nominated artistes are expected to join Mason and Green in announcing the nominees. They include Alan Menken, Amy Allen, Carly Pearce, David Guetta, FYÜTCH and Aura V, Herbie Hancock, Israel Houghton, Juanes, Kehlani, Linda Perry, Meghan Foley and Michelle Holme, Olivia Dean, Pharrell Williams, Renée Fleming, YUNGBLUD and Ziggy Marley. New Categories The 2027 edition introduces five new award categories, bringing the total number of categories to 100. They are Best Asian Pop Music Performance, Best Latin Song, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance, Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, and Best Traditional Folk Album. The eligibility period for the awards covers recordings released between August 31, 2025, and August 28, 2026. LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – FEBRUARY 01: (FOR EDITORIAL USE ONLY) Olivia Dean attends the 68th GRAMMY Awards at Crypto.com Arena on February 01, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.
